To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a rare pathological association was discovered in a case of pancreatic insulinoma.
we have reported a case of insulinoma with adenomatosis of Wirsung's pancreatic duct and chronic pancreitis in a woman.
the patient presented a secreting insulinoma with an endocrine hyper-plasia (possibly nesidioblastoses), a villous adenoma of the pancreatic duct, and a chronic pancreatitis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the pancreatic endocrine hyperplasias and adenomas.
a pancreatic insulinoma with a peritumoral hyperplasia of the endocrine cells.
a case of pancreatic insulinoma, adenocarcinoma and chronic pancreatitis in which immunohistochemical and ultrastructural investigations were carried out.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the insulinoma is a neoplasm which is not related to the chronic pancreatitis.
the insulinoma was the cause of the chronic pancreatitis and of the endocrine hyperplastic lesions.
the pancreatic insulinoma was the primary lesion, and the other lesions were secondary to it.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the association of a villous adenoma of the Wirsungs's duct and a secreting insulinoma is a very unusual association which may be explained by a possible neoplastic transformation of the endocrine hyperplastic foci of the adenomatous ducts.
the association of an insulinoma, a chronic pancreatite, an endocrine adenomatosis and a villous duct adenomatosis is possible in a case of hypoglycaemic syndrome.
a chronic pancreatitis can be associated with a secreting insulinoma and an endocrine adenomatosis of a pancreatic duct.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the diagnosis of insulinoma should be considered in the presence of an endocrine hyper-plasia and/or a pancreatic adenomatosis, even in the absence of a clear-cut hypoglycaemic syndrome.
the presence of insulinoma in patients with chronic pancreatitis and adenomatosis of Wirsung's pancreatic duct should be suspected.
a careful clinical examination, coupled with the appropriate tests and the right interpretation of the results, is necessary in order to avoid the risk of missing the diagnosis of an insulinoma.
